correctness.rationale: The proof derives all distances, identifies every and only MMD pair, reconstructs the strong resolution–vertex-cover equivalence, exhaustively classifies admissible mixed point/line complements using unique incidence, counts their sizes with a verified overlap subtraction, and classifies all maximal complements. The \(q\geq2\) inequality n > q+2 establishes precisely two bases. Standalone Python executed on the actual included path and reproduced all \(2^{14}\) direct strong-resolution tests for PG(2,2) and independent polynomial/maximal counts for PG(2,2) and PG(2,3). Finite checks corroborate but do not substitute for the universal proof.

value.rationale: The complete distribution of strongly resolving landmark sets, not just minimum size, is a natural combinatorial metric invariant of every projective-plane incidence graph. The universal formula is independent of coordinatization, including non-Desarguesian planes, and the inclusion-minimal family has a nontrivial exact two-level spectrum with an unbounded gap \(q^2-1\). This supports structural study of strong landmark redundancy and compares a stronger metric invariant with the extensively studied ordinary incidence resolution problem. It is not a one-off table, trivial renaming, or merely an exact computation.
